body.how: Contracts and side letters: sentence rules for change-of-control and convenience clauses, written by hand (no language model). The cyber assessment: one regular expression per finding line. Customers: names normalised (case, punctuation, legal suffixes, common abbreviations, a leading 'The') and matched exactly, else to the most similar name sharing the first word if similarity is at least 0.9.

simulation_truth.what: what the generator put in the data room; the parsers and the matcher never see it

comparables.what: the average latest disclosure of deals at least three years old that still disclose

body.how: Every deal in the database counts at each disclosure: log(reported / announced) = features . beta + k log(months / 36) + the deal's own effect + reporting noise, by maximum likelihood over the first-anniversary and latest reports. Deals that went quiet after their first year still contribute that year. Draws for this deal add coefficient uncertainty and the deal effect. ERP lateness: lognormal, with programmes still running as right-censored.

simulation_truth.what: the process the database was generated from; the fit never sees it

cost.note: announced share enters as a kink above 8%, relative size above 30%; the model is linear in both

body.how: Average-linkage clusters on the Jaccard distance between each application's functional tags, cut at 0.75; a cluster holding applications of both companies is an overlap. The baseline is matching on product name.

simulation_truth.what: each application's true capability, which the tags only hint at

sentences.text: Corvane Systems: $310M revenue over the last four quarters at a 14% EBITDA margin; the price of $1.20B carries a $260M premium over standalone value.
The largest customer is 15.1% of revenue and the ten largest 37%.
14 customers can end their contracts on a change of control, covering $115.4M of annual revenue (37%); the rules that found them miss wording that never names the event, so this is a floor.
3 critical or high cyber findings are open, 2 of them internet-facing; remediation is estimated at $2.2M on stated planning rates.
48% of revenue comes from customers the acquirer already serves, which the deal database says pulls revenue synergies down.
Against a case of $30M cost and $45M revenue synergies, the model fitted to the deal database expects $27.6M (80%: 20.8–36.3) and $12.5M (6.8–22.7).
ERP integration: fast (approved); expected synergy value $268M (80%: 194–350) against a $260M premium, a 51% chance of covering it; the plan as written says $397M.
After the latest quarterly reports, cost synergies are forecast at $29.6M and revenue synergies at $16.6M a year.
1 review task open: Revenue synergies forecast at 37% of the case after 4 quarters.
